To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the play of infants and toddlers is related to the child's cognitive development, language development, and attachment to the mother and that play assessment provides a window into the child's development.

(a) the quality of mother-child interaction is related to the infant's play, (b) infant play is correlated with later language and cognitive development, and (c) play is an indicator of the infant's cognitive competence and of the mother's sensitivity to her child's signals.

the infant's play behavior with objects is a good indicator of what the child understands about objects and that the child's play with people is a good indicator both of the child's understanding of people and of the child's attachment to the play partner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of play and with the relationship between play and other aspects of development.
the development of play in infants and toddlers.
the relationship between infant play and the infant's social, emotional, and cognitive development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
play assessment has been useful in the study of infant and toddler development and has been useful in practice.
play assessment is an important part of the nursing process.
play is an important part of the infant's life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the play assessment techniques we have used are useful and valid.
the more the mother is involved in play and the more the mother and child play together in a mutually positive manner, the better the child's development.
the more the mother-child interaction is marked by positive affect and by a sense of shared enjoyment, the more likely the infant is to develop the ability to engage in play.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nurses can use play as an important window to the child's developmental status and as a way to engage the child in a relationship.
play is a valuable tool for nurses in practice and in the research setting.
the assessment and measurement of infant and toddler play is an important tool for both researchers and clinicians to use.
